problem: Existing object-goal navigation methods focus on learning visual representations but ignore navigation-state quality; high correlation among historical navigation states (dominant past states) causes inefficient or failed navigation.
motivation: The authors observe that high relevance among consecutive navigation states leads to navigation inefficiency or failure. The agent needs to remain sensitive to current observation changes and not be dominated by history, so that it takes valid actions.
key_idea: HiNL estimates navigation states by exploring relations among historical states, with a History-aware State Estimation module that reduces dominant past states' influence and a History-based State Regularization loss that suppresses correlation between states during training.
insight: Abstract only: the paper claims that decorrelating navigation states (via HaSE at inference and HbSR at training) improves both success rate and SPL in unseen environments. No ablation details are available from the abstract, so the specific contribution of each component cannot be assessed.
method: History-aware State Estimation (HaSE): estimates the current navigation state from historical states while reducing the influence of dominant past states and staying alert to current observation changes
History-based State Regularization (HbSR): a training-time regularizer that explicitly suppresses correlation among navigation states
HiNL framework: history-inspired navigation policy learning combining HaSE and HbSR for object-goal navigation

setting.backbone: not specified in abstract (learned navigation policy)
setting.training_data: not specified in abstract; trained in AI2-THOR (iTHOR and RoboTHOR)

results: The abstract states that HiNL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on Success Rate and SPL in unseen test environments on iTHOR and RoboTHOR. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only evaluated in the AI2-THOR simulator (iTHOR/RoboTHOR); no real-robot results are mentioned
Full details are unavailable because only the abstract was provided
